newsitem.title: CHINA: Several China firms seen issuing convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: Several China firms seen issuing convertible bonds.

text.p: The first group of Chinese firms to issue corporate convertible bonds under a new quota could go to the market as early as October with several issues expected by the end of 1997, underwriters said on Monday.
China announced in April that up to four billion yuan worth of convertible bond issues would be allowed under a new quota.
Some of China's largest unlisted companies could offer bonds that would be convertible into stock, pushing these firms eventually to list shares, officials have said.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), China's top market regulator, has received applications from eligible firms and is now considering when to give the green light, a CSRC official told Reuters.
"The companies have applied (to issue convertible bonds)," she said. "We are considering now and will likely approve a group."
The official declined to say when the first batch of firms would start to issue convertible bonds, but underwriters have already started to divide up the pie.
"Nearly all the brokerages have secured a piece of the (convertible bond) underwriting business," said an official at Shenzhen J&A Securities Co Ltd.
"Several bonds will be offered within this year," the official said from the southern city of Shenzhen.

More than 100 companies have applied to issue convertible bonds but only around 20 have met the necessary requirements so far due to strict rules about their profits, size and management, said an official at China Southern Securities in Shenzhen.
Individual corporate convertible bond issues must be at least $100 million yuan.

China will draw mainly on its roughly 500 key state-owned enterprises to issue convertible bonds, an official from the State Economic and Trade Commission was quoted as saying by the China Daily on Monday.
Convertible bonds offer a way to ease fund shortages of state enterprises and develop the capital markets, the official said.

China has previously allowed a handful of companies to issue convertible bonds but most have been a flop with investors, mainly because the underlying shares have remained unattractive. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
